name: registry_recover
description: Replay the transaction logs (.LOG1, .LOG2) a registry hive was copied with onto a COPY of it, and read the key and value records of the result. A hive that was in use when it was copied is dirty (its two sequence numbers differ) and its newest state is in its logs; regkv reads the hive as it is. The logs are the ones you name: nothing is looked for beside the hive. The original and the logs are only opened for reading; the copy, a receipt and the records are written under work/<your id>/registry_recover-<id>/ (in a job, under $OUT). The replay follows the two log layouts (Suhanov's registry format specification; libyal's REGF notes) and does not use regipy's apply_transaction_logs, which writes every entry whatever its sequence number. New format (HvLE, Windows 8.1 and later): an entry is applied only when its signature and its two Marvin32 hashes are right and its sequence number is the one the hive needs next; an entry older than the hive's state, an entry that does not follow, and the log from an entry whose hash is wrong are NOT applied and are listed under `unrecovered` with the hive ranges their pages would have written. An entry is also NOT applied, whatever its hashes, when it lists no page, declares a hive bins data size that is not a positive multiple of 4096 or is more than the hive file's own bins plus 64 MiB (and 4 GiB), names a page that is not whole 512-byte sectors or lists more pages than its bins have sectors; the reason is under `unrecovered` and the scan stops at it. At most 50,000 entries of a log are scanned (about 2 KB each in memory; 122 MB measured with 50,001 entries none of which could be applied, and a receipt of 17 MB); the rest of the log is named in the receipt (`logs[].trailing`: where it starts and how many bytes) and is unrecovered. A long list of page references is listed as hive ranges up to 20,000 per entry and 200,000 in all; the rest are counted and named by their place in the log (`page_references`), where the log has them whole. The tool's own clock (max_seconds) is looked at while the hive, the logs and the recovered copy are hashed, while the log is scanned, while the pages hash is checked and while the pages are written (a hash the limit stopped is not made: the receipt names it under `not_hashed`, with the bytes that were read, and the status is partial); when it is reached the replay stops, no recovered copy is left, the entries that would have been applied are listed as not applied and the status is partial. Old format (a DIRT vector and dirty sectors): applied as a whole only when the log's own sequence numbers agree with each other and with the hive's primary number. A clean hive is not replayed; a log entry newer than a clean hive is reported, not applied. The recovered copy differs from the original in the pages of the applied entries and in the fields of its base block that the receipt names: both sequence numbers, the hive bins data size and the checksum always, and, for a new-format log, the root cell offset and the last-written time (taken from the base block of the log that holds the last applied entry) and the flags (those of that entry) where they differ; a log whose own base block checksum is wrong is not believed for them and the status is partial. An old-format log changes the first four only. It is a derivative: cite the original, the logs and this tool's version beside it. Records are read with regipy (keys.jsonl: path, name, depth, raw last-write FILETIME and ISO UTC, subkey and value counts, then each value with its type, size and raw data; changes.jsonl: what differs from the original when a replay applied something) and counted again by libregf's regfexport when it is installed: `independent_reader` says whether the counts agree, and a disagreement makes the status partial. regfexport is held to a ceiling: address space of a gigabyte and four times the hive, and output of 64 MiB and 64 times the hive (a damaged 8 KB hive made it take 5.5 GB and print 8 GB); when it passes one, fails or does not finish in time it is stopped, `why_not_finished` says which, its counts are not compared, and the status is partial. Not done: no other state than the one the logs lead to (earlier states are other sources), no repair of a hive that is damaged beyond its logs, no interpretation of values. A key name, a value name or a value data size that is longer than the cell it was read from is not followed into the next cell (regipy would read on, and a withheld value's bytes could end up in a path): the record's name becomes `[name withheld: ...]` with the hive offset and the numbers and none of the bytes, a value under such a name or such a key is withheld like a secret, a data size is cut at its cell, and each is a problem line (`records.problems`) that makes the status partial. SENSITIVE and withheld by shape: the V and SupplementalCredentials values of each SAM user, the values under the LSA secrets and cached-logon keys of a SECURITY hive, and any value whose name says password, secret, token or credential (a DWORD or QWORD excepted) are written as a record with their place, name, type and length, and not their bytes. `write_values: true` writes those values to values.jsonl with mode 0600 and is refused unless the tool runs as a job with secret_output: true; nothing is made when it is refused. A secret inside a value that does not look like one (a command line with a password in it) is not recognised and is written with the rest, so run the tool as a job with secret_output: true when the hive's content matters. Every answer carries status (complete, partial, failed) and status_basis; partial names what was not read or not applied. A hive larger than 4 GiB, a pipe or a device is not opened. Memory: the replay works in 1 MiB pieces and holds no page reference (about 50 MB resident for a 64 MiB hive and a 60 MB log, plus about 2 KB for each log entry scanned); reading the records is regipy's, which holds the whole hive in memory, so a 300 MiB hive was read at about 400 MB resident, and a hive or recovered copy over 512 MiB is replayed and not read (records.status skipped, with the reason, and the status partial). export: false skips the reading. It starts no program in a group of its own and ends regfexport with itself.

hive.description: The registry hive file (a copy of it). It is only opened for reading

log1.description: The .LOG1 transaction log of that hive (named; none is looked for)

log2.description: The .LOG2 transaction log of that hive

export.description: Write keys.jsonl (and changes.jsonl when a replay applied something) (default true). false replays and writes the receipt only

write_values.description: Write the values that are withheld to values.jsonl under $OUT, mode 0600 (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job with secret_output: true; the answer never carries a value

limit.description: Rows of keys.jsonl shown inline (default 200, an inline page size); every row is kept, and the whole result is in the file the answer names

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds, 1 to 110 (default 90); a read that reaches it stops, says so and is partial
